courses.name: Calculus I
courses.description: Limits, derivatives, and integrals of single-variable functions. Fundamental theorem of calculus. Applications to physics and engineering.

courses.name: Physics I: Mechanics
courses.description: Classical mechanics: kinematics, Newton's laws, work and energy, momentum, rotational motion, and oscillations. MATH101 must be taken concurrently.

courses.name: Introduction to Engineering
courses.description: Engineering disciplines, design process, problem-solving methods, technical communication, and ethics. Includes hands-on prototyping lab.

courses.name: Calculus II
courses.description: Integration techniques, series, sequences, polar coordinates, and an introduction to multivariable calculus.

courses.name: Physics II: Electricity & Magnetism
courses.description: Electric fields and potentials, Gauss's law, capacitance, DC circuits, magnetic fields, Faraday's law, and Maxwell's equations. MATH201 must be taken concurrently.

courses.name: General Chemistry
courses.description: Atomic structure, chemical bonding, stoichiometry, thermodynamics, and electrochemistry relevant to materials science.

courses.name: Differential Equations
courses.description: Ordinary differential equations: first and second order, systems of ODEs, Laplace transforms, and series solutions. Applications to mechanical systems.

courses.name: Linear Algebra
courses.description: Vector spaces, matrix algebra, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and linear transformations.

courses.name: Engineering Statistics
courses.description: Probability theory, statistical distributions, hypothesis testing, regression analysis, and design of experiments for engineering applications. Accepts MATH201 or MATH301 as prerequisite.

courses.name: Statics
courses.description: Equilibrium of particles and rigid bodies, free body diagrams, distributed forces, friction, centroids, and moments of inertia.

courses.name: Dynamics
courses.description: Kinematics and kinetics of particles and rigid bodies, Newton-Euler equations, work-energy methods, impulse-momentum, and vibrations introduction.

courses.name: Mechanics of Materials
courses.description: Stress, strain, deformation of axially loaded members, torsion, bending, shear, combined loading, and failure theories.

courses.name: Materials Science
courses.description: Crystal structure, phase diagrams, mechanical properties, failure modes, and selection criteria for metals, polymers, ceramics, and composites.

courses.name: Thermodynamics
courses.description: Laws of thermodynamics, thermodynamic properties of pure substances, work and heat interactions, power and refrigeration cycles.

courses.name: Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Fluid properties, hydrostatics, conservation equations, dimensional analysis, internal and external flows, and introduction to turbulence.

courses.name: Heat Transfer
courses.description: Conduction, convection, and radiation heat transfer. Steady-state and transient analysis. Heat exchangers and thermal systems design.

courses.name: Machine Design
courses.description: Fatigue, fracture mechanics, design of shafts, bearings, gears, fasteners, and welded joints. Failure mode and effects analysis.

courses.name: Vibrations
courses.description: Free and forced vibrations of single- and multi-degree-of-freedom systems, resonance, damping, modal analysis, and vibration isolation.

courses.name: Engineering Analysis
courses.description: Numerical methods for engineering analysis: root-finding, interpolation, numerical integration, ODEs, and finite element method introduction.

courses.name: Senior Capstone Design I
courses.description: First semester of two-semester capstone design project. Problem definition, literature review, concept generation, prototyping, and preliminary design review. Must be taken with ME451 concurrently.

courses.name: Senior Capstone Design II
courses.description: Second semester of capstone design. Detailed design, fabrication, testing, analysis, and final design presentation. Must be taken with ME450 concurrently.

courses.name: Technical Elective
courses.description: Departmental technical elective. Choose from advanced topics in thermal-fluids, design, or dynamics. Requires completion of at least one of: ME310, ME401, or ME320.
